title: How Iran’s drones hit America’s Achilles heel
author: @politico
text: How Iran’s drones hit America’s Achilles heelRecent threats on U.S. bases show just how unprepared the military is for drone warfare.By Paul McLeary and Victor Jack10/08/2026 5:00 AM EDTAdd POLITICO on Google Share XFacebookEmailRedditWhatsAppLinkedInThe abrupt evacuation of American bombers from a key U.K. airbase underscores the extreme vulnerability facing the world’s most powerful fighting force and its NATO allies — as cheap drones and off-the-shelf tech transform warfare.President Donald Trump has insisted Iran’s military is “completely destroyed” due to eight months of attacks from American and Israeli firepower. But Tehran continues to strike back with low-cost Shahed drones that have kept the Navy from returning to U.S.-friendly ports in the Middle East and severely damaged an American airbase near Iran. Warnings about Iranian drones even led to the evacuation of all U.S. bombers from Britain’s Fairford air base this week and sent Trump scurrying into a catering cart in July as he left a NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey.The actions underscore the pervasiveness of these new threats — and just how unprepared U.S. and European officials are to tackle a new kind of warfare.“What worries me is a growing possibility of ‘drone terrorism’ and ability of different semiorganized groups and vile individuals to act against our infrastructure by cheap, even household made, means,” said a senior European defense official.LoadingNational Security DailyFrom the SitRoom to the E-Ring, the inside scoop on defense, national security and foreign policy.
